CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Shared conventions

The portfolio’s shared rules (workflow, r-package, ci, correctness, assurance) come from the r-skills plugin’s rules/, loaded at session start because of the marker above. Never copy them here. Where this file and a shared rule disagree, this file wins for this package. Cloud sessions do not load the plugin and run without them.

What this is

zulake opens a Delta Lake table where it is stored (Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 or Blob Storage, or local disk) and exposes everything the table’s log records as base data frames: versions, commits, live files with their partition values, statistics and deletion vectors, schema, protocol and properties, and the changes between versions. Reading data, with file pruning by partition and statistics, is the convenience on top. It is pure R over zujson, qio and zuhttp, with zuroar suggested for deletion vectors. It does not write, run queries, obtain Azure tokens or support stores other than Azure, and 0.1.0 does not read Iceberg.

The specification is .agents/design.md, adopted from RFC 0081. It outranks this file: CLAUDE.md orients, the design decides.

Current state

Scaffolded 2026-11-26 with create-pkg.sh; no functionality yet. The roadmap in .agents/roadmap.md takes it to v0.1.0. 0.1.0 waits for zuhttp on CRAN and for zuroar 0.1.0 (design §9); local log replay, inspection and reading are built on local fixtures first.

Versions and dependents

v0.1.0 issue: created by pkg-roadmap. Sibling packages that will depend on this one: zugodb, through an extension that registers a delta format (design §3).

Commands

Only the shared commands so far.

Architecture

To be written as stages land; see .agents/design.md. There is no native layer: no src/, by design (D1).

Invariants that are easy to break

  • No compiled code (D1). The log is JSON and Parquet, which zujson and qio read; adding src/ changes the package’s CI and CRAN profile.
  • zulake never imports zugodb (D6). zugodb calls zulake; the reverse makes a dependency cycle.
  • The bearer token never leaves the request. It is not stored in a snapshot, printed, or included in an error or a recorded cassette (D4, acceptance criterion 4). A leak here is a credential leak.
  • Unknown or unsupported reader features are refused by name before any data is read (D7). Ignoring columnMapping in id mode or deletion vectors returns wrong rows silently.
  • Statistics only decide what is downloaded. A file is pruned only on “cannot match”; the whole filter is then applied to rows, so a read is exact whatever the statistics say (design §6).
  • Names are for a table, not for Delta (D11). The lake_ functions, the snapshot class and the data frames they return must take Iceberg later without renaming.

Testing

None yet: no conformance suite, helpers or runtime measured. The design (§8) plans DAT and delta-rs fixtures, deltalake 1.7.0 as the oracle in a development-only workflow, and a live Azure suite gated on ZULAKE_AZURE_URI.

Continuous integration

R-CMD-check.yaml calls r-actions r-cmd-check.yml@v1; coverage.yaml calls r-actions coverage.yml@v1 (badge on gh-pages); pkgdown.yaml builds and deploys the site. cran-release.yaml calls r-actions cran-release.yml@v1 when CRAN-SUBMISSION is pushed: it tags the submitted commit, creates the GitHub release and opens the .9000 bump. So CRAN-SUBMISSION is committed, not ignored. No package-specific workflows yet.
